newsitem.title: KENYA: Nairobi bourse stable, bond trading suspended.
newsitem.headline: Nairobi bourse stable, bond trading suspended.

text.p: Low demand at the Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) held the 20-share index steady in a moderately active market, brokers and bourse officials said on Monday.
The index went up 0.04 points to stand at 3042.10. Turnover was posted at 7.816 million shillings traded on 216,430 shares from 53.773 million shillings traded on 1,388,140 shares.
Brokers said activity was concentrated on the foreign board while trading on the normal board was very quiet.
November saw foreign investors dominate buying in the market, suppporting prices on some shares like Kenya Commercial Bank, Firestone East Africa, and Kenya Breweries.

"It looks like our local investors are as depressed as our market has been," one broker said. "They keep saying the sustained low prices of shares like Kenya Airways, has discouraged them from active trading in the market."
Kenya Commercial Bank traded at 62.50 unchanged, while Kenya Breweries traded at 52 from 51.50. Kenya Airways closed at 8.95 from 8.90, while Rea Vipingo Plantations traded at 10.55 from 10.50.
Power monopoly Kenya Power & Lighting eased to 136 from 138, while Firestone East Africa closed at 28.50 from 26.
"Kenya Power appears to be undercapitalized. It looks attractive now that a lot of money is being pumped into it, to try and make it generate funds for improvement from within," another broker said.

"Actually ever since the price jumped to 116 sometime this year, Kenya Power's share price has never been the same. But I think it is not because of anything conspicuous, but rather a simple question of demand," a senior broker said.

The much awaited trading of corporate bonds at the Nairobi bourse did not take place. An official at the NSE said it had been moved forward, hopefully to December 5, so as to put up necessary facilities for trading to take place.
"It was realized that we cannot use the same clearing system for corporate bonds as we do for equities," he added.
Many brokers said they did not really understand the procedures for trading bonds in the secondary market -- "It still is a grey area to many of us," one broker said.
